messages.author: 508f3eb35c142863
messages.subject: Moderation in Lavaan
parts:
Hello everybody,

In my master thesis I look at the stability of personality traits, using a latent moderated regression in the R-Packet Lavaan. However, I always get an error message when adding the interaction terms from the items and the gender and the mean-centered age. I hope you can help me

I created my interaction terms with indProd ().

I then used these to define latent variables in the SEM.

Here is my script:

Masterdatensatz <- indProd(Masterdatensatz, var1="Bigfive1_v", var2="Geschlecht" , var3=NULL,          match = FALSE, meanC = TRUE, residualC = FALSE, doubleMC = TRUE, namesProd = NULL)

Masterdatensatz <- indProd(Masterdatensatz, var1="Bigfive7_v", var2="Geschlecht" , var3=NULL,          match = FALSE, meanC = TRUE,  residualC = FALSE, doubleMC = TRUE, namesProd = NULL)

Masterdatensatz <- indProd(Masterdatensatz, var1="Bigfive11_v", var2="Geschlecht" , var3=NULL,        match = FALSE, meanC = TRUE,  residualC = FALSE, doubleMC = TRUE, namesProd = NULL)

Masterdatensatz <- indProd(Masterdatensatz, var1="Bigfive1_v", var2="Alterc" , var3=NULL, match =                   FALSE, meanC = TRUE,  residualC = FALSE, doubleMC = TRUE, namesProd = NULL)

Masterdatensatz <- indProd(Masterdatensatz, var1="Bigfive7_v", var2="Alterc" , var3=NULL, match =                   FALSE, meanC = TRUE, residualC = FALSE, doubleMC = TRUE, namesProd = NULL)

Masterdatensatz <- indProd(Masterdatensatz, var1="Bigfive11_v", var2="Alterc" , var3=NULL, match                    = FALSE, meanC = TRUE, residualC = FALSE, doubleMC = TRUE, namesProd = NULL)

 

model_extra.r1 <-

  't1 =~ 1*Bigfive1_v + b*Bigfive7_v + c*Bigfive11_v

t2 =~ 1*Bigfive1_n + b*Bigfive7_n + c*Bigfive11_n

PRTM =~ 1*Bigfive1_v.sex +b* Bigfive7_v.sex + c*Bigfive11_v.sex

PRTA =~ 1*Bigfive1_v.agec + b*Bigfive7_v.agec + c*Bigfive11_v.agec

# residual covariance

Bigfive1_v ~~ Bigfive1_n

Bigfive7_v ~~ Bigfive7_n

Bigfive11_v ~~ Bigfive11_n

 

t2 ~ t1 + sex + agec + PRTM + PRTA

'

fit_extra.r1 <- sem(model_extra.r1, Masterdatensatz)

summary(fit_extra.r1, fit.measures = TRUE)

 

The errors I see are:

 

Warning messages:

1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  :

  lavaan WARNING: some observed variances are (at least) a factor 1000 times larger than others; use varTable(fit) to investigate

2: In lav_object_post_check(object) :

  lavaan WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negative

3: In lav_object_post_check(object) :

  lavaan WARNING: some estimated lv variances are negative

 

Is it because of my data or what I have programmed.

 

In the work I have to add other interactions between life events and the first measurement time, which makes the whole SEM even more complex. I determine the interactions again with indProd (). I get the same error messages. It would be great, if you could help me. I am desperate.

 

Best regards

Mira

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Moderation in Lavaan
parts:
Hi Mira,

The first warning might be driving everything you're seeing. ML estimation gets "finicky" when variables are on very different scales (e.g. variances differ by a factor of 100 or 1000). My guess the issue is that the products you're using are the culprits. I'd look at the variances in the data and see which variables have (very) large and small variances. Then consider if you can rescale the variables to be on similar scales (I'd do the rescaling first and then recompute the product terms).

Alex

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Moderation in Lavaan
parts:
Standardization is a rescaling method, but one I probably wouldn't recommend (since you're then treating an estimate of a Sd as a known population SD). Rescaling might be as easy as dividing the variable(s) on the largest scale by 10.

Standardizing categorical variables doesn't make a ton of sense to me. I'd only rescale the variables with the largest variances. 

Having categorical variables as moderators might be leading to the other errors too. All the work on product indicator approaches I've seen assumes the indicators are continuous. If you have a single categorical variable that you believe is a mediator then it would be easier to use a multiple group approach to testing the interactions instead of a product indicator approach.
